name: Hall sensors and reed switches
summary: Magnetic sensors: Hall-effect chips and glass reed switches that detect a nearby magnet.
uses: Counting wheel or shaft turns (speed, flow)
identify: Reed switches are tiny glass tubes with two metal reeds, inside door and window alarm contacts, float switches, bike speed sensors and laptop lids. Hall sensors are small three-legged chips in BLDC motors, e-bike throttles, flow meters and brushless fans.
test: Reed: continuity changes when a magnet comes close. Hall: power it with 5V and the output pin flips when a magnet passes.
